otu_data=read.delim2("NII_Abundance_custom_point1.tsv",sep = "\t",header = TRUE, row.names = 1)

my_taxa=tax_table(taxa_data)
my_meta=sample_data(meta_data)
ps_NII=phyloseq(my_otu,my_taxa,my_meta)
ps_NII

alpha_measurement=c("Shannon")
richness_estimate=estimate_richness(PS_NII, measures = alpha_measurement)
## Warning in estimate_richness(PS_NII, measures = alpha_measurement): The data you have provided does not have

## estimates (for example) are probably unreliable, or wrong, if you have already
## trimmed low-abundance taxa from the data.

my_comparisons=list(c("Non-Tumor","Tumor"))
p=ggboxplot(richness_estimate,x="Sample_Type",y="Shannon",
            color = "Sample_Type", palette = "jco",
            add = "jitter")
p=p+stat_compare_means(comparisons = my_comparisons)+stat_compare_means(label.y = 4.5)
p

#Boruta to identify features
my_taxa_names=as.data.frame(tax_table(PS_NII))
taxa_names(PS_NII)=my_taxa_names$Species
pseq_df <- as.data.frame(t((phyloseq::otu_table(PS_NII))))
pseq_df$Sample_Type <- phyloseq::sample_data(PS_NII)$Sample_Type%>%as.factor()

library(Boruta)
set.seed(123456)
sig_taxa=Boruta(Sample_Type~., data = pseq_df, pValue=0.05,mcAdj = TRUE, maxRuns=999)
print(sig_taxa)
## Boruta performed 303 iterations in 2.639751 secs.
##  3 attributes confirmed important: Acinetobacter lwoffii, Micrococcus luteus, uncultured Stenotrophomonas sp.;
##  377 attributes confirmed unimportant: [Clostridium] innocuum, [Clostridium] symbiosum, [Eubacterium] siraeum,
## [Ruminococcus] lactaris, [Ruminococcus] torques and 372 more;
sig_UR_df <- attStats(sig_taxa)
getSelectedAttributes(sig_taxa)
## [1] "Acinetobacter lwoffii"           "uncultured Stenotrophomonas sp." "Micrococcus luteus"
boruta_fixed <- TentativeRoughFix(sig_taxa)
## Warning in TentativeRoughFix(sig_taxa): There are no Tentative attributes! Returning original object.
getSelectedAttributes(boruta_fixed)
## [1] "Acinetobacter lwoffii"           "uncultured Stenotrophomonas sp." "Micrococcus luteus"
boruta_physeq=prune_taxa(getSelectedAttributes(boruta_fixed),PS_NII)

symnum.args = list(cutpoints = c(0, 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 1),
                   symbols = c("Wilcoxon, p= 0", "Wilcoxon, p= 0.0001", "Wilcoxon, p= 0.001", "Wilcoxon, p= 0.01", "Wilcoxon, p > 0.05"))

a_my_comparisons <- list( c("Non-Tumor","Tumor"))




phyloseq::psmelt(boruta_physeq) %>%
  ggplot(data = ., aes(x = Sample_Type, y = log(Abundance))) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, aes(x=Sample_Type, color=NULL, fill=Sample_Type, alpha=0.05)) +
  geom_jitter(aes(color = OTU), height = 0, width = .2) +
  labs(x = "", y = "log Abundance\n") +
  facet_wrap(~ OTU, scales = "free_x") +
  stat_compare_means(method = "wilcox.test", comparisons = a_my_comparisons, label = "p.signif", symnum.args = symnum.args,label.y = 8.0)+
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5),strip.text = element_text(size = 15))+theme_classic()

#run wilcoxon test for significance of DA taxa
library(gapminder)
library(modelr)
library(tidyverse)
wilcox_model <- function(df){
  wilcox.test(abund ~ Sample_Type, data = df)
}
wilcox_pval <- function(df){
  wilcox.test(abund ~ Sample_Type, data = df)$p.value
}
#Create nested data frames by OTU and loop over each using map 
wilcox_results <- pseq_df %>%
  gather(key = OTU, value = abund, -Sample_Type) %>%
  group_by(OTU) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(wilcox_test = map(data, wilcox_model),
         p_value = map(data, wilcox_pval))  
## Warning: There were 758 warnings in `mutate()`.
## The first warning was:
## ℹ In argument: `wilcox_test = map(data, wilcox_model)`.
## ℹ In group 1: `OTU = "Acetivibrio ethanolgignens"`.
## Caused by warning in `wilcox.test.default()`:
## ! cannot compute exact p-value with ties
## ℹ Run `dplyr::last_dplyr_warnings()` to see the 757 remaining warnings.
head(wilcox_results)

# Calculate Bray-Curtis distances
dist_matrix <- distance(PS_NII, method = "bray")

# Extract patients with BOTH Tumor and Non-Tumor samples
patient_groups <- table(sample_data(PS_NII)$Patient, sample_data(PS_NII)$Sample_Type)
patients_with_pairs <- rownames(patient_groups)[
  rowSums(patient_groups[, c("Tumor", "Non-Tumor")] > 0) == 2
]

cat("Patients with paired Tumor/Non-Tumor:", length(patients_with_pairs), "\n")
## Patients with paired Tumor/Non-Tumor: 18
patient_distances <- data.frame()

for(patient in patients_with_pairs) {
  # Get sample indices for this patient
  patient_samples <- sample_data(PS_NII)$Patient == patient
  tumor_samples <- patient_samples & sample_data(PS_NII)$Sample_Type == "Tumor"
  nontumor_samples <- patient_samples & sample_data(PS_NII)$Sample_Type == "Non-Tumor"
  
  if(sum(tumor_samples) > 0 & sum(nontumor_samples) > 0) {
    # Extract pairwise distances
    tumor_dist <- as.matrix(dist_matrix)[tumor_samples, nontumor_samples]
    
    # Create data frame
    pairs_df <- expand.grid(
      tumor_sample = sample_names(PS_NII)[tumor_samples],
      nontumor_sample = sample_names(PS_NII)[nontumor_samples],
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
    pairs_df$bray_distance <- as.vector(tumor_dist)
    pairs_df$Patient <- patient
    
    patient_distances <- rbind(patient_distances, pairs_df)
  }
}

  theme_classic()  +coord_flip()

#simple code to find taxa not seen in any non-tumor smaples but seen in at least a few tumor samples
library(phyloseq)
library(dplyr)

# Subset samples
ps_tumor <- subset_samples(ps_NII_rel_abund, Sample_Type == "Tumor")
ps_nontumor <- subset_samples(ps_NII_rel_abund, Sample_Type == "Non-Tumor")

# Get taxa names present in each group (counts > 0 in at least one sample)
taxa_tumor <- taxa_names(subset_taxa(ps_tumor, taxa_sums(ps_tumor) > 0))
taxa_nontumor <- taxa_names(subset_taxa(ps_nontumor, taxa_sums(ps_nontumor) > 0))

# Tumor-only taxa
tumor_only_taxa <- setdiff(taxa_tumor, taxa_nontumor)

# View results (e.g., at Species level; adjust rank)
tax_table(PS_NII)[tumor_only_taxa, "Species"]

# Extract OTU/ASV table
mat <- as(otu_table(ps_tumor_only), "matrix")

# Ensure taxa are rows (phyloseq can store either way)
if (!taxa_are_rows(ps_tumor_only)) {
  mat <- t(mat)
}
# Convert to relative abundance
mat_rel <- sweep(mat, 2, colSums(mat), "/")

# Or log transform (adds stability)
mat_log <- log10(mat + 1)
tax <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps_tumor_only))

# Example: label rows with Genus + Species
rownames(mat_rel) <- paste(tax$Genus, tax$Species, sep = "_")
heatmap(mat_rel)

install.packages("ComplexHeatmap")
## Error in install.packages : Updating loaded packages
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(circlize)

# Example matrix
mat <- mat_rel  # or mat_log, depending on what you're using

# Define color mapping: 0 = white
col_fun <- colorRamp2(
  c(0, 0.01, max(mat)),   # breakpoints
  c("white", "lightblue", "darkblue")
)

Heatmap(mat,
        name = "Abundance",
        col = col_fun)
